opportunities.title: [Bounty: $80] Add tests for payloads exceeding bodySizeLimit returning 413
opportunities.summary: ## Context `src/app.ts` configures `express.json({ limit: securityConfig.bodySizeLimit })` (default `1mb`). A larger payload makes body-parser throw an `entity.too.large` error with `err.status = 413`, which `errorHandler` currently converts into a 500 because it ignores `statusCode` on non-`AppError` errors. ## Proposed Change Add a supertest that sends a >1mb body to a POST route (e.g. `/api/v1/agents`) and asserts the response is 413 rather than 500, and that the error envelope stays consistent. ## Acceptance Criteria - Test sends an oversized body and asserts status 413 - Test asserts `success: false` in the response body - Test documents the expected error-handler behavior change ## Suggested Label tests

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $75] Add tests for malformed JSON bodies returning a 400 error
opportunities.summary: ## Context When a client sends malformed JSON to `POST /api/v1/agents` or `POST /api/v1/payments/quote`, the `express.json()` body parser in `src/app.ts` throws a `SyntaxError` carrying `err.status = 400` and `err.type = 'entity.parse.failed'`. `errorHandler` in `src/common/http/error.middleware.ts` only special-cases `AppError`, so this currently surfaces as a 500 with the raw parser message. ## Proposed Change Add supertest cases that post invalid JSON (e.g. `{"name": "x"`) to `/api/v1/agents` and assert the response is 400 with the standard error envelope (`success: false`), pinning the expected behavior before the handler is fixed. ## Acceptance Criteria - A test posts malformed JSON and asserts status 400 - The response body matches the `ApiErrorResponse` shape - The test fails before the 400-handling fix and passes after ## Suggested Label tests

opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
